# A customer and a vendor carrying a key this tool has no setter for.
#
# Anything the format does not know is kept in a slot beside the object and
# written back out on export, so a ledger can carry a field this tool does not
# understand and not lose it.
#
# Removing such a key has to land, and has to be said: a block that leaves
# the line out is not asking for anything, because most blocks state only
# what they are changing and a printed invoice states less than that. Writing
# the slot from the block regardless made every partial block a delete;
# writing it only when the block stated something meant the last key could
# never be removed. Stating it `$None$` says which was meant.
#
# an_owner_with_a_custom_key.txt is this file with the key.
#
# Each states the key `$None$`, which is how a key is removed; `""` would be
# the empty text. Leaving the line out says nothing about it.
#
# What this fixture produces: the same objects, with the key removed.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_removing_a_custom_key_removes_it_from_the_book.py.
2026-01-01 commodity CAD
	mnemonic: "CAD"
	fullname: "Canadian Dollar"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 100

customer "C-KEY"
	name: "Acme Supplies"
	currency: CAD
	department: $None$

vendor "V-KEY"
	name: "Beta Printing"
	currency: CAD
	department: $None$

2026-01-01 open Income
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Income:Sales
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

invoice "INV-KEY"
	customer_id: "C-KEY"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-01-01
	department: $None$
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-01
		description: "A line"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
